# Helm / Kubernetes standard

## Summary

- Charts pass `helm lint`, render with `helm template` and validate with `kubeconform -strict`.
- Every configurable value is documented in `values.yaml` and typed in `values.schema.json`.
- Workloads are secure by default: non-root, read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation, resource requests and limits.
- No secrets in charts or values; reference existing Secrets.
- Chart tests (`helm unittest`) cover each spec scenario.

## Structure

- Keep the chart layout the repo already has. Templates live in `templates/`, helpers in `_helpers.tpl`.
- Name templates `<chart>.<thing>` in `_helpers.tpl`; use `include`, not `template`.
- Use the standard labels (`app.kubernetes.io/name`, `instance`, `version`, `component`, `part-of`, `managed-by`) via one helper.
- Bump `version` in `Chart.yaml` for every chart change (SemVer); `appVersion` tracks the application.

## Values and schema

- `values.yaml` holds safe defaults and a comment for every key.
- `values.schema.json` types every value, marks required ones and sets bounds (`minimum`, `enum`, `pattern`). Adding a value means updating the schema in the same change.
- Never remove or rename a value without a deprecation path; consumers depend on it (it is a contract).
- Quote strings in templates (`{{ .Values.x | quote }}`); use `required` for mandatory values.
- Use `toYaml` with `nindent` for nested structures; keep whitespace control (`{{-`) consistent.

## Workload security

- `securityContext`: `runAsNonRoot: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, drop all capabilities.
- Set resource requests and limits; define liveness and readiness probes.
- Pin images by tag from values (digest preferred); never `latest` in defaults for production charts.
- Least-privilege RBAC: namespaced `Role` over `ClusterRole`, only the verbs needed.
- No `hostPath`, `hostNetwork` or privileged containers unless the task requires them.

## Secrets and config

- Never put secret values in `values.yaml`, templates or tests; reference Secrets by name.
- ConfigMaps for non-secret configuration; checksum annotations to roll pods on change.

## Testing

- `helm unittest` suites in `tests/*_test.yaml` per template; assert on rendered fields, not whole documents.
- CI value files in `ci/*-values.yaml` for alternative configurations; each must render and validate.
- Every spec scenario maps to at least one test whose name mentions the scenario.

## Anti-patterns

- Hard-coded namespaces, names or image tags in templates.
- Values without schema entries; untyped `values.schema.json` (`additionalProperties` everywhere).
- Logic-heavy templates that belong in the application.
- Breaking value renames without deprecation.

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `tests/*_test.yaml`
- `*/tests/*_test.yaml`
- `ci/*-values.yaml`
- `*/ci/*-values.yaml`

## Gates (defaults; the repo's own scripts and config overrides win)
- format: `yamllint {charts}`
- lint: `helm lint {charts}`
- types: `for c in {charts}; do helm template "$c" | kubeconform -strict -summary || exit 1; done`
- test: `helm unittest {charts}`
- testAffected: `helm unittest {charts}`

# Python standard

## Summary

- Modern, fully typed Python; code passes the repo's type checker in strict mode.
- `ruff` formats and lints; follow PEP 8 naming and the repo's layout.
- Explicit errors with specific exception types; never a bare `except`.
- `pytest` tests with plain `assert`, fixtures for setup, one behaviour per test.
- Dependencies come from the locked environment (`uv`); no ad-hoc installs.

## Naming and structure

- `snake_case` for functions, variables and modules; `PascalCase` for classes; `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants.
- Keep the package layout the repo already has (`src/` layout or flat). No new top-level packages for a single use.
- Modules expose a small public surface; prefix internals with `_`.
- No logic at import time beyond constants and definitions. Entry points use `if __name__ == "__main__":` or a console script.
- Prefer functions and dataclasses (`@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`) over classes with mutable state.

## Types

- Annotate every public function, method and module-level variable.
- Use built-in generics (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`) and `X | None`.
- Use `typing.Protocol` for structural interfaces; avoid `Any`. Narrow with `isinstance`.
- Validate external data at the boundary (pydantic or the repo's validator) and pass typed objects inward.
- `# type: ignore` needs an error code and a reason.

## Errors

- Raise specific exceptions (built-in or a small project hierarchy); never `raise Exception`.
- Catch the narrowest exception you can handle; never `except:` or `except Exception: pass`.
- Chain with `raise ... from err` when translating errors.
- Use context managers (`with`) for files, locks, connections and temp dirs.

## Idioms

- Comprehensions for simple transforms; plain loops when there is logic.
- `pathlib.Path` instead of `os.path`; f-strings for formatting; `logging` instead of `print` in library code.
- Use the standard library first (`itertools`, `functools`, `collections`, `datetime` with time zones).
- No mutable default arguments.

## Security

- Never pass untrusted input to `eval`, `exec`, `pickle`, `yaml.load` (use `safe_load`) or `subprocess` with `shell=True`.
- Parameterise SQL. Use `secrets` for tokens, not `random`.
- Never log secrets or personal data. Read configuration from the environment or the repo's settings module.

## Testing

- `pytest` only; test files `test_*.py` under `tests/` (mirror the package layout).
- Plain `assert`; `pytest.raises` for errors; `pytest.mark.parametrize` for tables of cases.
- Fixtures for setup, `tmp_path` for files, `monkeypatch` for env; mock only process boundaries.
- Every spec scenario maps to at least one test whose name mentions the scenario.

## Anti-patterns

- Bare `except`, broad `except Exception` without re-raise.
- Mutable default args, star imports, global mutable state.
- Untyped public functions; `Any` leaking through APIs.
- Reformatting or reordering untouched code.

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `test_*.py`
- `*/test_*.py`
- `*_test.py`
- `tests/*`
- `*/tests/*`
- `conftest.py`
- `*/conftest.py`

## Gates (defaults; the repo's own scripts and config overrides win)
- format: `ruff format --check .`
- lint: `ruff check .`
- types: `pyright` (with pyrightconfig.json); or `pyright` (when pyproject.toml has [tool.pyright]); or `mypy --strict .`
- test: `pytest`
- testAffected: `pytest {testFiles}`

# React standard

Applies on top of the TypeScript standard.

## Summary

- Function components and hooks only; components are pure functions of props and state.
- Follow the Rules of Hooks; effects synchronise with external systems and nothing else.
- Accessible by default: semantic HTML, labels, keyboard support (jsx-a11y clean).
- Test with Testing Library through what the user sees; no snapshot-only tests.

## Components

- One exported component per file, named like the file, in `PascalCase`.
- Type props with an explicit `interface Props` or `type Props`; no `React.FC`.
- Keep components small. Extract a component when a piece has its own state or is reused, not to shorten a file.
- Derive values during render instead of storing them in state. State holds the minimum needed.
- Lift state only as far as needed; prefer composition (children, render props) over prop drilling through many layers.
- Lists need stable keys from the data, never the array index for reorderable lists.

## Hooks and effects

- Call hooks unconditionally at the top level of components and custom hooks.
- `useEffect` is for synchronising with something outside React (subscriptions, timers, DOM APIs). Do not use it to derive state or to react to prop changes that can be computed during render.
- Every effect that subscribes must clean up.
- Dependency arrays are complete; fix the code instead of silencing `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`.
- Use `useMemo`/`useCallback` only for measured costs or referential stability that a child or effect needs.
- Custom hooks start with `use` and encapsulate one concern.

## Data and side effects

- Fetching goes through the repo's data layer (e.g. React Query, router loaders); do not invent a new one.
- Handle loading, error and empty states explicitly.
- Never put secrets in client code; treat everything shipped to the browser as public.
- Avoid `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; if unavoidable, sanitise with the repo's sanitiser and explain why.

## Accessibility

- Use the right element (`button` for actions, `a` for navigation, `label` for inputs).
- Every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard and has an accessible name.
- Images have meaningful `alt` text or `alt=""` when decorative.
- Do not convey information by colour alone.

## Testing

- Testing Library: query by role, label or text (`getByRole` first); avoid test ids unless nothing else fits.
- Interact with `user-event`, assert on visible outcomes.
- Mock the network at the boundary (e.g. MSW), not internal hooks or components.
- No snapshot-only tests. A snapshot may complement explicit assertions, never replace them.

## Anti-patterns

- State that mirrors props; effects chained to update state from other state.
- Index keys on dynamic lists; components defined inside other components.
- Disabling `react-hooks` or `jsx-a11y` lint rules.
- Global mutable stores for local UI state.

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `*.test.ts`
- `*.test.tsx`
- `*.spec.ts`
- `*.spec.tsx`
- `*.test.js`
- `*.test.jsx`

- `*/test/*`
- `*/tests/*`

# Rust standard

## Summary

- `cargo fmt` formatting and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean.
- `Result`-based error handling with `?`; no `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests and proven invariants.
- Ownership first: borrow instead of clone, make illegal states unrepresentable with types.
- No `unsafe` unless the task requires it, with a `// SAFETY:` comment per block.
- Unit tests in `tests.rs` submodules, integration tests in `tests/`.

## Naming and structure

- `snake_case` for functions, variables and modules; `UpperCamelCase` for types and traits; `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for constants.
- Keep the crate/workspace layout the repo already has. Keep modules small and focused.
- Minimal public API: `pub(crate)` by default, `pub` only for the crate's interface.
- Derive common traits (`Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`, …) where they make sense.
- Prefer enums and newtypes over booleans and raw primitives for domain values.

## Errors

- Libraries define error enums (`thiserror` if the repo uses it); binaries may use `anyhow` with `.context(...)`.
- Propagate with `?`; add context where the error crosses a boundary.
- `unwrap()`/`expect()` only in tests or with a comment proving the invariant.
- Never `panic!` for recoverable conditions.

## Ownership and performance

- Take `&str`/`&[T]` parameters instead of `String`/`Vec<T>` when ownership is not needed.
- Avoid needless `.clone()`; restructure borrows instead.
- Use iterators and their adapters; collect only when needed.
- Avoid `Rc<RefCell<…>>` webs; prefer clear ownership or message passing.

## Concurrency and async

- Use the async runtime the repo already uses; never block inside async code (`spawn_blocking` for blocking work).
- Shared state behind `Arc<Mutex<…>>`/`RwLock` with short critical sections; never hold a lock across `.await`.

## Security

- No `unsafe` without a documented invariant; prefer safe abstractions from std or existing deps.
- Use parameterised queries; `std::process::Command` with arguments, never a shell string with untrusted input.
- Do not log secrets or personal data.

## Testing

- Unit tests: declare `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` and put them in `tests.rs` next to the module, so tests live in their own files.
- Integration tests under `tests/` against the public API.
- One behaviour per `#[test]`, named after it; use `assert_eq!` with messages for non-obvious values.
- Every spec scenario maps to at least one test whose name mentions the scenario.

## Anti-patterns

- `unwrap()` in library code, `clone()` to silence the borrow checker.
- Stringly-typed APIs; `Box<dyn Error>` in library interfaces.
- `#[allow(clippy::…)]` without a reason.
- Large `unsafe` blocks; blocking calls in async functions.

## Test paths (tester edit scope)
- `tests/*`
- `*/tests/*`
- `*/tests.rs`
- `benches/*`
- `*/benches/*`

## Gates (defaults; the repo's own scripts and config overrides win)

- lint: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- types: `cargo check --all-targets`
- test: `cargo test --workspace`
- testAffected: `cargo test {crates}`

# TypeScript / JavaScript standard

## Summary

- Strict TypeScript: `strict`, no `any`, no non-null assertions; narrow `unknown` instead.
- Validate every external input (HTTP, files, env, JSON) at the boundary with a schema.
- Small modules with named exports; pure functions where possible; no hidden global state.
- Errors are typed and handled where they can be acted on; never swallowed.
- Tests sit next to the code (`*.test.ts`) and test behaviour, not implementation.

## Naming and structure

- `camelCase` for values and functions, `PascalCase` for types, classes and React components, `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` only for true constants.
- One concept per module. Prefer named exports; default exports only where a framework requires them.
- Keep the module structure the repo already has. Do not introduce new layers (services, managers, utils barrels) for a single use.
- Use `import type` for type-only imports. No circular imports.
- Prefer `const`; `let` only when reassigned; never `var`.

## Types

- No `any`. Use `unknown` plus narrowing, generics, or a schema-derived type.
- Model states with discriminated unions instead of optional-field soup.
- Prefer `readonly` arrays and properties for data that is not mutated.
- Derive types from schemas (`z.infer`) or from `as const` objects; don't duplicate them by hand.
- Avoid `as` casts. A cast needs a one-line comment explaining why it is safe.
- Use `satisfies` to check object literals without widening.

## Errors

- Throw `Error` subclasses with a clear message; never throw strings or plain objects.
- Catch only where you can recover, add context, or translate the error at a boundary.
- Always handle promise rejections: `await` every promise or return it; no floating promises.
- Use `try/finally` (or `using`) to release resources.
- Do not log and rethrow the same error at every layer.

## Async and performance

- Run independent awaits concurrently with `Promise.all`; keep dependent ones sequential.
- Do not block the event loop with synchronous I/O in request paths.
- Avoid N+1 calls in loops; batch where the API allows it.

## Security

- Never build shell commands, SQL or HTML by string concatenation with untrusted input.
- Use parameterised queries and the platform's escaping.
- Never log secrets, tokens or personal data.
- Do not disable TLS verification or add `eval`/`new Function`.
- Pin dependencies through the lockfile; do not add a dependency for something the standard library or an existing dependency already does.

## Testing

- Use the repo's runner (vitest, jest or `bun test`). Match its file naming.
- One behaviour per test, named after the behaviour ("returns 404 when the user is missing").
- Arrange-act-assert; no logic (loops, conditionals) in tests.
- Mock only at process boundaries (network, clock, filesystem), never the unit under test.
- No snapshot-only tests: assert on the values that matter.
- Every spec scenario maps to at least one test whose name mentions the scenario.

## Anti-patterns

- `any`, `// @ts-ignore`, `// eslint-disable` without a reason.
- Barrel files that re-export everything; deep relative imports across packages.
- Catch-all `catch (e) {}` blocks; returning `null` and `undefined` interchangeably.
- Classes with only static methods; singletons holding mutable state.
- Reformatting untouched code in the same change.
